title: Fynaptix · Space Economy Research
heading: Space Economy Intelligence
subheading: Launch, satellites, constellations & the post-SpaceX-IPO landscape
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Space is capital-intensive with heavy government-customer concentration. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Global space economy estimated at ~$626B in 2026; Goldman Sachs and McKinsey both project a climb to $1.8T by 2035 alongside a rising wave of sector M&A

kpis.sub: BELOW POST-IPO HIGH · STARSHIP FLIGHT 14 STILL NET SEPT 15-30
kpis.label: SPCX climbed further to ~$149.74 by Sept 4 — well above its $135 IPO price — but remains ~34% below its $225.64 post-IPO high; Starship Flight 14 (first orbital attempt, first Ship tower-catch, first Starlink V3 delivery) is still targeted for a NET Sept 15-30 window after Ship 41 completed a full-duration, six-engine static fire on Aug 21

kpis.sub: 2026 YTD STARTUP FUNDING · STOKE SPACE CLOSES $1B SERIES E
kpis.label: Crunchbase-tracked global private investment in space/satellite startups held at a record $20.3B for 2026 as of late August — already the highest annual total on record with four months still to go; Stoke Space closed its Series E at roughly $1B on Aug 21 (~$9B valuation ex-new-money) while Rocket Lab continues drawing on its $3.6B Iridium bridge facility

kpis.sub: RKLB BACKLOG VS. STOCK BELOW THE IRIDIUM COLLAR FLOOR
kpis.label: Rocket Lab's record Q2 backlog reached $2.36B — bolstered by an Aug 4 $397M Space Force Flatellite (SB-AMTI) award on top of the NITE-STAR and Space Data Network wins — yet shares closed at $64.29 on Sept 4, a market cap of ~$38.5B, now trading below (not just testing) the $67.50 floor of the Iridium exchange-ratio collar, locking in the deal's fixed 0.4000 exchange ratio

tiers.label: Scale Players
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: Q2 revenue $7.8B (+92% YoY), with Starlink/connectivity revenue up 66% YoY to $4.3B (~$17B annualized) and 12M subscribers, adding 500k+ new subs a month; connectivity remains the only profitable segment ($1.66B operating profit). Shares climbed to ~$149.74 by Sept 4 — well above the $135 IPO price — still ~34% below the $225.64 post-IPO high
rows.watch for: Starship Flight 14 — first orbital attempt, first tower-catch of Ship, first Starlink V3 delivery — still NET Sept 15-30 after Ship 41's full-duration, six-engine static fire on Aug 21; four more share-unlock tranches through Dec 8, 2026; Starlink ARPU down 22% YoY as international/lower-priced plans scale

rows.angle: Record Q2 revenue of $234M (+62% YoY) and a record $2.36B backlog, padded by an Aug 4 $397M Space Force Flatellite (SB-AMTI) award on top of the NITE-STAR/Space Data Network wins; guided Q3 revenue to $250-265M and still targets a mid-2027 Iridium close. Neutron has logged 400+ Archimedes hot fires with a full engine set built for the first launch, still tracking to Q4 2026 pad delivery
rows.watch for: Shares closed at $64.29 on Sept 4 — now trading below, not just testing, the $67.50 floor of the Iridium exchange-ratio collar, which locks in the fixed 0.4000 ratio; Morgan Stanley raised its bull-case target to $293 and ARK Invest has reportedly been buying shares in early September, but Neutron's maiden flight remains unflown and free cash flow isn't expected to turn positive until 18-24 months after first flight

rows.angle: Sam Mehta is now several weeks into the President & CEO role following the Aug 17 Kubasik ouster; FY26 guidance remains intact and L3Harris demonstrated multi-domain capability at the Aug 18 Project Convergence exercise. Still building 18 of the SDA's Tranche 3 tracking satellites under the $1.75B AMDT3 award (with Sierra Space)
rows.watch for: Law firm Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman opened a securities-claims investigation tied to the Kubasik ouster, adding a fresh legal overhang on top of Deutsche Bank's Aug 18 price-target cut to $268; shares near $262.82, about 44% below the $379.23 52-week high; also sits in the Defense sleeve — don't double-count exposure

tiers.label: Growth / Speculative
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

Q2 sales rose to $31.5M on a reaffirmed $150-200M FY26 guide
rows.watch for: Shares rallied to ~$62.12 (market cap ~$24.3B) after last week's 15.5% rate-driven drop; still building its constellation largely on borrowed money, and the $1B convertible-note dilution overhang and BlueBirds 14-16 shipping timeline remain the swing factors

rows.angle: Booked a Sept 1 order for two new IM 300 platforms from an undisclosed new customer, extending diversification beyond lunar landers alongside the $600M+ GEO satellite contract, the JPL-selected EAGLE-VSWIR mission, the Tranche 3 missile-defense build with L3Harris, and the Goonhilly/COMSAT acquisitions. Shares traded in a $14.56-$14.97 range on Sept 4
rows.watch for: Integration execution on Goonhilly/COMSAT; wider-than-expected Q2 loss (-$0.29/sh vs -$0.10 est.); IM-3 Nova-C lander assembly progress; mission binary risk remains structurally unchanged

rows.angle: Q2 revenue of $116.1M (+58% YoY) delivered Planet's first profitable quarter as a public company; shares popped to ~$19.51 in after-hours trading against a 10-analyst Buy-consensus target that has since moved to ~$34.90
rows.watch for: Next-quarter guidance of ~$103M came in roughly 10% below estimates, and the stock has round-tripped from its $51.76 May high; the profit print is encouraging but not yet enough to close the analyst-target gap

rows.angle: Record Q2 revenue of $117.1M (+89.6% YoY), record 27.8% gross margin, and a record $542.1M backlog (book-to-bill 1.42); announced a new phased-array antenna investment (Aug 25) and a 164,000-sq-ft Huntsville expansion adding ~150 jobs by 2027, backed by ~$8.5M in incentives
rows.watch for: BofA raised its price target to $8 from $7 on Aug 31 — still below the ~$10.50 quote (market cap ~$2.7B), a mixed signal even as fundamentals keep improving; sustaining margin gains as revenue scales remains the key watch item

private_watchlist.name: Blue Origin
private_watchlist.note: Root cause of the May 28 New Glenn pad explosion (a BE-4 main oxygen valve) remains under remediation at ULA's Decatur plant and Cape Canaveral, with NASA Stennis hot-fire testing set to begin this fall. Building out Pad 36A plus a second Cape Canaveral pad (36B), a new Vertical Integration Facility, and a government-partnered Payload Processing Facility for the larger New Glenn 9x4. Company remains "very committed" to a return to flight by year-end.

private_watchlist.name: Firefly Aerospace
private_watchlist.note: Record Q2 2026 revenue of $117.7M (+659% YoY, first quarter above $100M) on a record $1.5B backlog (95% of FY26 guidance already booked), alongside a $92.3M net loss; the quarter included a $144M NASA CLPS lunar-lander award, a $75M NASA JPL MoonFall subcontract, a $94M Space Force radar-digitization contract, and a two-year Lockheed Martin extension. Shares trade around $21.53, well off their highs after Roth Capital's Aug 17 price-target cut to $45 from $60 on valuation concerns.

private_watchlist.name: Stoke Space
private_watchlist.note: Closed its Series E at roughly $1B on Aug 21 at a ~$9B valuation ex-new-money, on top of the $1.34B already raised, while expanding Moses Lake test facilities and activating Cape Canaveral's LC-14. First Nova liftoff still targeted for end of 2026.

bear_case.title: Capital intensity
bear_case.description: Rockets and constellations burn billions before returns — Stoke Space's Series E closed at ~$1B on Aug 21 on top of $1.34B already spent pre-launch; dilution and debt are chronic among small caps (RKLB's $3.6B Iridium bridge facility, ASTS's $1B convertible notes), and ASTS is only now recovering from a 15.5% single-day drop on Fed rate-hike chatter — a reminder of how exposed debt-funded builders are to the rate cycle even as this week's rally shows sentiment can turn just as fast.

bear_case.title: Government concentration
bear_case.description: Much of the sector's revenue is NASA/DoD — the SDA's Golden Dome build-out (L3Harris/Sierra Space's $1.75B Tranche 3 award, RKLB's $397M Flatellite and $981M NITE-STAR ceiling) keeps flowing, but a securities-claims investigation now sits alongside the Aug 17 CEO ouster at prime contractor L3Harris, a reminder that governance and sentiment risk sit alongside budget risk in this concentrated customer base.

bear_case.title: SpaceX absorbs the value / sector repricing
bear_case.description: A dominant incumbent with launch-cost leverage can compress everyone else's margins — SPCX has climbed to ~$149.74 but remains ~34% below its post-IPO high, and its next real catalyst (Starship Flight 14) is still NET Sept 15-30. Meanwhile record fundamentals across RKLB, RDW, LUNR and Firefly this earnings season haven't stopped RKLB shares from trading below the $67.50 floor of its own Iridium collar — a widening gap between operating results and price that cuts both ways.

bear_case.title: Binary mission risk
bear_case.description: One failed test or delayed launch can halve a small-cap, or push a manifest by months: Starship Flight 14 remains NET Sept 15-30 even after Ship 41's full-duration six-engine static fire, Rocket Lab's Neutron still hasn't flown despite 400+ hot fires, and Blue Origin's BE-4 root-cause finding shows how fast hardware failure can stall a program ahead of its promised year-end return to flight. SpaceX's own prospectus flags "key man" dependence on Elon Musk.
